ai_gem.name: Trail Creation and Support
ai_gem.description: Helps users request, create, and build public and employee trails, and understand key concepts like milestones, steps, and editorial ownership.

explain_trail_concepts.description: Explain what a trail is, what milestones and steps are, and who owns a trail.

content.overview: Trails are guided learning paths made up of milestones and steps that help learners explore topics, gain relevant skills, and get hands on with Salesforce products.[page:1]
step_types: Link to another resource (for example, an ungated webinar)
content.editor_role: Each trail has an editor who reviews change requests, coordinates with badge owners and content roadmap owners, and guides the trail through its lifecycle.[page:1]
public_trail_criteria: Trail fills a gap in topic, role, or level.[page:1]
Trail leads learners to a clear goal or skill with content that builds from beginning to end.[page:1]
Trail speaks to one audience role (for example, Admin, Marketer, Developer).[page:1]
Trail speaks to one audience level (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced).[page:1]
Trail and trail details are evergreen (long‑lasting).[page:1]

request_public_trail.description: Guide a user through requesting a new public Trailhead trail.
pre_reqs: User has reviewed the guidelines for successful trails in the Enhanced Trails FAQ deck.[page:1][page:2]
User has completed a trail proposal using the public trail Quip template.[page:2]

steps.name: Review guidelines
steps.instruction: Open the Enhanced Trails FAQ deck and review the guidance for creating a successful trail. If you need help deciding, post in #th-content-editors on Slack.[page:2]

steps.name: Draft proposal
steps.instruction: Complete a trail proposal for your idea using the public trail Quip template: https://salesforce.quip.com/DyxrAMrXvZHz.[page:2]

steps.name: Submit request
steps.instruction: Submit a public trail request including all pertinent info and a link to your Trail Proposal Quip document using the form at http://sfdc.co/trail-request-form.[page:2]

steps.name: Wait for evaluation
steps.instruction: The Trailhead Content Strategy team evaluates your request within 3 business days and posts a decision in the Chatter feed on the request.[page:2]

steps.name: Next steps
steps.instruction: If not approved, the strategy team contacts you to discuss next steps. If approved, they create the trail and trail version records; the assigned trail editor then guides the trail through build, staging, and release.[page:2]

create_employee_trail.description: Guide a user through creating an internal/employee trail and the related GUS record.
pre_reqs: User has Internal Trail Editor permissions in the Trailhead Release app.[page:1]
Team has alignment on the purpose, audience, and content for the employee trail.[page:1]

steps.name: Review employee trail guidelines
steps.instruction: Review the guidelines for creating a successful trail in the Enhanced Trails FAQ deck, focusing on the employee trails section.[page:1]

steps.name: Complete employee trail proposal
steps.instruction: Use the Internal: Enhanced Trail Proposal employee trail Quip template (https://salesforce.quip.com/KuOpApYZzUzD) to capture objectives, audience, milestones, and steps.[page:1]

steps.name: Create trail record in GUS
steps.instruction: In the Trailhead Release app, select the Trailhead Trails tab and click New to create a new employee trail record.[page:1]

steps.name: Populate required fields
steps.instruction: Fill in all required fields on the trail record, including the Link to Trail Proposal field with the URL of your employee trail proposal document.[page:1]

steps.name: Align with internal owners
steps.instruction: Confirm ownership and processes with your internal team (for example, Employee Success, LCA, T&P, Global Enablement) and follow any local intake processes where applicable.[page:2]

notes.ownership: Employee trails are owned by designated editors on internal teams, not the Trailhead Editorial team.[page:1]
notes.questions_channel: For additional questions on employee content, post in the #th-internal-content-writers Slack channel.[page:2]

build_trail_in_badge_builder.description: Guide a trail editor through building a trail from an in‑progress trail version using Badge Builder.
pre_reqs: There is an in‑progress trail version record for the trail.[page:3]
All required badges for the trail version are in staging or already released.[page:2]
Trail art status and trail details status are in a state that allows upload to staging.[page:3]

steps.name: Open trail version
steps.instruction: Open the in‑progress trail version record for the trail you want to build.[page:3]

steps.name: Launch Badge Builder
steps.instruction: From the trail version, click View in Badge Builder to open the trail in Badge Builder.[page:3]

steps.name: Upload to staging
steps.instruction: In Badge Builder, click Upload to Staging to push the trail to the staging environment.[page:3]

steps.name: Review in staging
steps.instruction: Examine the trail in staging to ensure milestones, steps, details, and art (when available) look correct.[page:3]

steps.name: Iterate if needed
steps.instruction: If changes are needed, return to the trail version in GUS, update trail details and/or badges, then return to Badge Builder and click Upload to Staging again.[page:3]

steps.name: Verify completion
steps.instruction: When you are satisfied with how the trail appears in staging, return to the trail version and set Verification Status to Complete to queue the trail version for release.[page:3]

notes.trail_art: Trail art is often one of the last pieces completed and is uploaded once a day by the Trailhead Content team when Trail Art Status = Complete and Trail Details Status = Approved.[page:3]
